sectorSummary.overview: Growth improves across the reviewed IT and technology calls, supported by AI-led work, larger engagements and deeper customer relationships. Coforge, Mphasis and Sagility upgrade parts of their outlook, while acquisition effects, investment costs and uneven demand leave profitability and cash conversion mixed.

trends.text: AI is moving into client workflows, platforms and delivery processes, with companies seeking measurable business outcomes.
Existing customer expansion and larger or more strategic engagements support the growth pipeline.

tailwinds.text: Reusable AI capabilities and productivity improvements support delivery efficiency and operating leverage.

headwinds.text: Selective client spending, slower decisions or weak pockets of demand limit the breadth of growth.
Hiring, wage revisions, integration or platform investment create near-term profitability pressure.

opportunities.text: Acquisitions and the proposed ITC Infotech combination expand capabilities and customer access, subject to integration or approvals.
Healthcare workflow automation and provider services offer additional areas for growth.
Tata Technologies is winning full-vehicle programs while developing aerospace as another growth engine.

risks.text: DSO, delayed collections and transaction-related cash payments need monitoring alongside reported growth.
Acquired revenue, adjusted profit and reported profit use different bases; headline growth does not establish organic growth or cash generation.
Large-deal conversion and customer adoption determine how quickly the pipeline becomes revenue.

insights.text: Coforge raises its FY27 EBIT-margin target to 16%, Mphasis lifts its growth outlook to low double digits, and Sagility raises its adjusted EBITDA-margin band to 25–26%.
Persistent’s operating PAT grows while reported PAT declines after Nagarro transaction costs; Nagarro had not closed at the call.
Intellect’s SaaS customer migration and Tata Technologies’ license-recognition change affect revenue comparability.
